judgment_text:
Prayer : Criminal Revision Petition filed under Section 438 & 442 of BNSS Act, 2023 (397 & 401 of Cr. P.C.,) to call for the entire records relating to Crime No.160/2025 on the file of the respondent police and set aside the order of dismissal dated 24.02.2026 passed by the Hon'ble Special Court under NDPS, Salem in Crl.M.P.No.89/2026 in Crime No.160/2025 on the file of the respondent police and direct the respondent to return the trailer vehicle bearing Reg.No.TN04 BB 8263 along with empty International container bearing No.SKHU920779-6 to the petitioner.

ORDER

1. The revision challenges the dismissal of the petitioner's application seeking the return of his Trailer vehicle bearing Reg. No. TN04 BB 8263, which was seized during the course of the investigation in Crime No. 160 of 2025 registered for the offences under Sections 8(c) r/w 20(b)(ii)(c), 25, 29(1) of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 and Section 123 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023.

2. It is the case of the prosecution that the accused in the said case was transporting 4 kg of Ganja inside the cabin of the said Trailer vehicle bearing Reg. No. TN04 BB 8263 along with an empty International container bearing No. SKHU920779-6 and thus committed the offences under Sections 8(c) r/w 20(b)(ii)(c), 25, 29(1) of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985 and Section 123 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023.

3. During the course of the investigation, the petitioner's vehicle, which was used by the accused, was seized. The petitioner sought return of the vehicle, which came to be dismissed by the impugned order.

4. The learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the petitioner is the owner of a Logistic Finn by the name of Tristar Logistics; that he has a vehicle, namely, a trailer bearing Reg. No. TN04 BB 8263; that when the vehicle was in charge of the eighth accused, who was a driver under the petitioner, an FIR was registered against him under Sections 8(c) r/w 20(b)(ii)(c), 25, 29(1) of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985, and Section 123 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 in Crime No. 160 of 2025, by the Vadavanakkambadi Police Station; and that 4 kg of contraband was recovered from the cabin of the vehicle.

4.1 The learned counsel for the petitioner would further submit that the trial court though has arrived at a conclusion that the vehicle stands in the name of Tristar Logistics, dismissed the application on the premise that there is a possibility of using this vehicle again for a similar nature of offence. He would further submit that the petitioner is not an accused; and that he is the owner of the vehicle, and therefore he is entitled for interim custody of the vehicle on any stringent conditions.

5. The learned government advocate (Crl.Side) confirmed the fact that the petitioner is not an accused in this case; that he is the owner of the vehicle; and that confiscation proceedings have been initiated.

6. At this juncture, the learned counsel for the petitioner relies upon the judgment of the Supreme Court, in Denash v. State of Tamil Nadu reported in 2025 SCC OnLine SC 2276 where the Supreme Court, has held that since because there is a hypothesis of suspicion for using the vehicle for very same nature of offence once again cannot be ground to deny the return of vehicle. The learned counsel would further rely upon the judgment of the learned Single Judge, held in Crl.R.C. No. 2877 of 2025, dated 8-1-2026 in A.Kailangiri v. The State, wherein this Court, referring to the judgment of the Denash ” case (cited supra) has released the vehicle with conditions.

7. Accordingly, considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and that the petitioner being the owner of the vehicle and not an accused, this Court is inclined to grant interim custody of the vehicle to the petitioner subject to the result of the confiscation proceedings on the following conditions:

(i) The petitioner shall execute a personal bond for a sum of Rs.5,00,000 (Rupees Five Lakhs Only) with two sureties for a likesum to the satisfaction of the learned Additional District Judge, Special Court under NDPS, Salem;

(ii) The petitioner shall produce the original RC Book along with a self-attested Photostat copy of the RC Book of the vehicle and other relevant records to prove his ownership. The learned Additional District Judge, Special Court under NDPS Salem, shall peruse the RC book and other records, retain a xerox copy of the same and return the original RC book to the petitioner;

(iii) The petitioner shall not alter or alienate the vehicle in any manner;

(iv) The petitioner shall also give an undertaking that he will produce the vehicle as and when required by the respondent and by the Court below;

(v) The return of property would be subject to the result of the confiscation proceedings.

8. Accordingly, this Criminal Revision Case stands allowed.
